claims.claim: Severian was Bishop of Gabala in Syria.
Severian flourished from around 400 until 404 as a popular preacher in Constantinople.
Severian was born in Syria and spoke Greek with a Syriac accent.
Severian came to Constantinople around 400, or in 398 or 399.
Severian became the enemy of John Chrysostom and helped condemn him at the Synod of the Oak.
The Fragmenta in epistulam ad Colossenses survives in catena tradition.
Severian was described by Gennadius as 'in Divinis Scripturis eruditus, et in Homiliis declamator admirabilis' (learned in the Divine Scriptures and an admirable declaimer in homilies).
Severian's interpretation of Colossians can be compared to contemporary authors to shed light on his contribution to Christian exegetical scholarship.
